findings.reason: The mechanics hold: parse_link_destination.mjs:52 now breaks without advancing, and link.mjs:76 then sees `\` instead of `)` and falls back to a reference, where the baseline (`pos++; continue`) kept the backslash and produced a link. But story.md is not in the packet and the new line matches upstream markdown-it, so I can't tell whether this narrower behaviour was asked for. Kept at medium (X1 said high) because the inputs affected are rare edge cases.
findings.claim: Breaking at a backslash followed by a space leaves pos on the backslash, so inputs like `[x](foo\ )` or a reference definition ending in `\ ` are no longer parsed as links.
findings.evidence: Line 52, `if (str.charCodeAt(pos + 1) === 0x20) { break }`, leaves `pos` on the backslash. lib/rules_inline/link.mjs:76 then sees `\` where it expects `)` and falls back to a reference lookup, so the link is never built. CommonMark spec example (test/fixtures/commonmark/spec.txt:500) says a backslash before a non-punctuation character such as a space is a literal backslash, so the destination should be `a\` with href `a%5C`. The baseline line `pos++; continue` kept the backslash and stopped at the space, so it produced that link. story.md is not in the packet, so I can't check whether this narrower behaviour was asked for. It does match upstream markdown-it.
